assertions: Before any edit to sizes.py, the trace shows a pytest run in which a test fails because a size at an exact unit boundary is formatted in the smaller unit (such as "1024.0 KB" or "1024 B").
A new test is added for an exact boundary other than 1048576 bytes (for example 1024 bytes expecting "1.0 KB"), and its name describes the behavior rather than a bug or ticket number.

The fix in sizes.py changes the loop comparison so that every unit boundary is handled (for example size >= 1024) rather than adding a special case for 1048576 or for MB, and the final response states this root cause.
The four original test functions in tests/test_sizes.py keep their names and assertions, no dependency is added to pyproject.toml, and the last pytest run in the trace passes with no failures.
